chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris narrated from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Musa, who said:

We went out with Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) to some of his properties on a day when there was no cloud. When we emerged, he said: 'Have you taken umbrellas with you?' We said: 'No, and what need do we have for an umbrella when there is no cloud and we do not fear rain?' He said: 'But I have taken one, and you will be rained upon.' He said: So we did not go far until a cloud rose, and we were rained upon until it troubled us, and none of us remained except that he was soaked.

key_terms.الرِّضَا: Al-Rida (the Accepting One), a title of the eighth Imam

ai.seo_question: What is the story of Imam al-Rida predicting rain on a clear day?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, this hadith highlights the Imam’s *karamat* (extrasensory gifts) as a sign of his divine leadership (*Imamah*), specifically his knowledge of the unseen (*ilm al-ghayb*) granted by Allah. The sudden, heavy rain on a cloudless day serves as a tangible miracle for his companions, reinforcing the Shia belief in the infallible Imams' unique spiritual authority and connection to the Divine Will.
